Dispatch case D11, morning. Produce an implementable plan for every listed pickup. Each stop ID must appear exactly once across all ordered vehicle routes. Output one JSON object only. Format {"routes":{"V01":[480,12,5],"V02":[490,4]}} where the first integer is departure minute since midnight (480 is 08:00), then only pending pickup IDs. Omit vehicles with no new pickups. The given current origin is implicit. Every used vehicle returns to depot 0. An already active unused vehicle returns to depot at its ready time. All operating times below are integer minutes since midnight. Vehicles can leave any time at or after ready. Drive, wait if early, then complete loading no later than the pickup deadline. Add load at every stop and stay under all three capacities. Use an allowed vehicle kind only. Return to depot by the shift deadline. Feasibility comes first. Then minimize cost in cents: new vehicle fixed costs plus distance at the vehicle's cents/km plus departure-to-return minutes at its cents/min. Existing active vehicles have no additional fixed cost. For a vehicle already active, charge time from its ready minute even if it waits before leaving. If a lookup asks for more than 72 directed legs, only the first 72 will be answered. Use the factual travel data below. Drives are directional and rounded up to minutes. If necessary you may first ask for up to 72 exact directed legs using only {"lookup":[["van",0,12],["box",5,4]]}. You get one lookup batch, after which you must return routes. Do not use code, shell, web, or other tools. The accompanying picture, when present, gives the same stop IDs. The output is scored by replay, so count every pickup and check equipment, loading, time and return.
